title: Aggregates and consistency boundaries
summary: An aggregate is a cluster of objects saved as one unit behind a single root that is the only path in for any change, so an invariant spanning several objects can never be broken from outside.
signals: a child entity (a line, an item, a slot) with its own repository or collection that callers query and update directly
a cached total, count or summary field that a rule spanning several child rows is supposed to keep correct, updated only when a caller remembers to
a collection getter that returns the live internal list or map, so callers can append, remove or mutate its elements directly
an invariant that spans more than one row (max count, sum, cross-field state) enforced nowhere, or re-checked separately in every caller

roles.Order (before): a header row: identity plus a cached total, no say over its lines
roles.OrderLine (before): a child entity with its own repository — reachable and mutable from anywhere
roles.Order (after): aggregate root: the only entry point for reading or changing a line
roles.OrderLine (after): held inside the aggregate; only copies of it ever leave
roles.OrderRepository (after): one repository per aggregate — saves and loads the whole Order, never a line by itself

stages.title: A child entity with its own repository
stages.idea: OrderLine has its own repository, so a caller can add an 11th line, zero out a quantity, or edit a line on a cancelled order without the Order ever finding out — and its cached total goes stale.

stages.title: Order as the aggregate root
stages.idea: Order is the only entry point (addLine, changeQuantity, cancel); lines are never reachable for mutation from outside; cancel enforces that a shipped or already-cancelled order can't be cancelled again; one repository saves and loads a detached copy of the whole aggregate; the total is always derived, never cached.

checks: Why does putting a repository on OrderLine make it possible to break a rule that spans several lines, like "at most 10 lines"?
Why does the aggregate return copies of its lines instead of the live objects it holds internally?
What single property must be true of every write that goes through Order, no matter which method is called?
Why is 'one repository per aggregate' a consequence of the boundary, not an arbitrary rule?
